newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chart Pattana party will be willing to join the next coalition if it is given complete control of economic portfolios. Party leaders say the party wants to run the key economic portfolios to revive trade and investment fast and effectively. (BANGKOK POST)

- Much of the ancient capital of Ayudhya is under water but palaces and historical ruins are being protected ahead of the visit by the British Monarch. Earthen dykes have been built and thousands of sandbags placed around the sites in preparations officials expect to complete ahead of the visit. (BANGKOK POST)

- A train station on the planned Bangkok subway has been relocated to the other side of a road following complaints from the Dusit Thani Hotel that it would have been forced to close down during construction at the old site. Agreement was reached during talks at Government House yesterday. (THE NATION)

- Thai shrimp exporters are expected to be hardest hit by ruling from the U.S. Court of International Trade, which ruled in favour of an environmental group and ordered U.S. officials to prohibit the import of any shrimp or shrimp products from Thailand. The ruling is expected to deliver a serious blow to Thai shrimp exports, worth more than 22 billion baht annually. (KRUNG THEP THURAKIJ)

- The Attorney General's Office has decided to prosecute former Bangkok Bank of Commerce president and three other associates who have been accused of embezzling 1.657 billion baht from the bank. (THE NATION) (KRUNG THEP THURAKIJ) (THE NATION)

- The Association of Finance Companies has joined U.S.-based Equifax Financial Services to establish the first central credit bureau in Southeast Asia. A final agreement for the venture is due by the end of the year, with operations to begin one year later. BANGKOK POST)
